CPDV.displayText: And you have thrown me into the deep, in the heart of the sea, and a flood has encircled me. All your whirlpools and your waves have passed over me.

verses.context: Praying from inside the great fish, Jonah recalls being thrown into the sea as the current swirled and the waves swept over him.

KJV.text: Then I said, I am cast out of thy sight; yet I will look again toward thy holy temple.
KJV.displayText: Then I said, I am cast out of thy sight; yet I will look again toward thy holy temple.

BSB.text: At this, I said, ‘I have been banished from Your sight; yet I will look once more toward Your holy temple.’
BSB.displayText: At this, I said, ‘I have been banished from Your sight; yet I will look once more toward Your holy temple.’

CPDV.text: And I said: I am expelled from the sight of your eyes. Yet, truly, I will see your holy temple again.
CPDV.displayText: And I said: I am expelled from the sight of your eyes. Yet, truly, I will see your holy temple again.

verses.context: Still inside the fish, Jonah admits he felt cast out of God's sight, yet says he will look again toward God's holy temple.

KJV.text: I went down to the bottoms of the mountains; the earth with her bars was about me for ever: yet hast thou brought up my life from corruption, O Lord my God.
KJV.displayText: I went down to the bottoms of the mountains; the earth with her bars was about me for ever: yet hast thou brought up my life from corruption, O Lord my God.

BSB.text: To the roots of the mountains I descended; the earth beneath me barred me in forever! But You raised my life from the pit, O LORD my God!
BSB.displayText: To the roots of the mountains I descended; the earth beneath me barred me in forever! But You raised my life from the pit, O LORD my God!

CPDV.text: I descended to the base of the mountains. The bars of the earth have enclosed me forever. And you will raise up my life from corruption, Lord, my God.
CPDV.displayText: I descended to the base of the mountains. The bars of the earth have enclosed me forever. And you will raise up my life from corruption, Lord, my God.

verses.context: Continuing his prayer from the fish's belly, Jonah recalls sinking to the roots of the mountains before God brought his life up from the pit.

KJV.text: And should not I spare Nineveh, that great city, wherein are more than sixscore thousand persons that cannot discern between their right hand and their left hand; and also much cattle?
KJV.displayText: And should not I spare Nineveh, that great city, wherein are more than sixscore thousand persons that cannot discern between their right hand and their left hand; and also much cattle?

BSB.text: So should I not care about the great city of Nineveh, which has more than 120,000 people who cannot tell their right hand from their left, and many cattle as well?”
BSB.displayText: So should I not care about the great city of Nineveh, which has more than 120,000 people who cannot tell their right hand from their left, and many cattle as well?”

CPDV.text: And shall I not spare Nineveh, the great city, in which there are more than one hundred and twenty thousand men, who do not know the difference between their right and their left, and many beasts?”
CPDV.displayText: And shall I not spare Nineveh, the great city, in which there are more than one hundred and twenty thousand men, who do not know the difference between their right and their left, and many beasts?”

verses.context: After Jonah grieves over a shade plant that withered, God asks him whether he should not care even more about the people of Nineveh.

KJV.text: I will bear the indignation of the Lord, because I have sinned against him, until he plead my cause, and execute judgment for me: he will bring me forth to the light, and I shall behold his righteousness.
KJV.displayText: I will bear the indignation of the Lord, because I have sinned against him, until he plead my cause, and execute judgment for me: he will bring me forth to the light, and I shall behold his righteousness.

BSB.text: Because I have sinned against Him, I must endure the rage of the LORD, until He argues my case and executes justice for me. He will bring me into the light; I will see His righteousness.
BSB.displayText: Because I have sinned against Him, I must endure the rage of the LORD, until He argues my case and executes justice for me. He will bring me into the light; I will see His righteousness.

CPDV.text: I will carry the wrath of the Lord, because I have sinned against him, until he may judge my case and execute judgment for me. He will lead me into the light. I will behold his justice.
CPDV.displayText: I will carry the wrath of the Lord, because I have sinned against him, until he may judge my case and execute judgment for me. He will lead me into the light. I will behold his justice.

verses.context: Speaking for his humbled people to a gloating enemy, Micah says they will bear God's anger for their sin until God brings them into light.

KJV.text: For all people will walk every one in the name of his god, and we will walk in the name of the Lord our God for ever and ever.
KJV.displayText: For all people will walk every one in the name of his god, and we will walk in the name of the Lord our God for ever and ever.

BSB.text: Though each of the peoples may walk in the name of his god, yet we will walk in the name of the LORD our God forever and ever.
BSB.displayText: Though each of the peoples may walk in the name of his god, yet we will walk in the name of the LORD our God forever and ever.

CPDV.text: For all people will walk, each one in the name of his god. But we will walk in the name of the Lord our God, forever and ever.
CPDV.displayText: For all people will walk, each one in the name of his god. But we will walk in the name of the Lord our God, forever and ever.

verses.context: After describing a future when nations stream to God's temple to learn his ways, Micah says his people will walk with the Lord forever.

KJV.text: In that day, saith the Lord, will I assemble her that halteth, and I will gather her that is driven out, and her that I have afflicted;
KJV.displayText: In that day, saith the Lord, will I assemble her that halteth, and I will gather her that is driven out, and her that I have afflicted;

BSB.text: “On that day,” declares the LORD, “I will gather the lame; I will assemble the outcast, even those whom I have afflicted.
BSB.displayText: “On that day,” declares the LORD, “I will gather the lame; I will assemble the outcast, even those whom I have afflicted.

CPDV.text: In that day, says the Lord, I will gather together the lame. And I will recover her whom I had rejected, and her whom I had afflicted.
CPDV.displayText: In that day, says the Lord, I will gather together the lame. And I will recover her whom I had rejected, and her whom I had afflicted.

verses.context: Through Micah, God promises that a day is coming when he will gather the lame, the scattered and the hurting of his people.

KJV.text: But thou, Beth–lehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.
KJV.displayText: But thou, Beth–lehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.

BSB.text: But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, who are small among the clans of Judah, out of you will come forth for Me One to be ruler over Israel— One whose origins are of old, from the days of eternity.
BSB.displayText: But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, who are small among the clans of Judah, out of you will come forth for Me One to be ruler over Israel— One whose origins are of old, from the days of eternity.

CPDV.text: And you, Bethlehem Ephrata, are a little one among the thousands of Judah. From you will go forth he who shall be the ruler in Israel, and his landing place has been set from the beginning, from the days of eternity.
CPDV.displayText: And you, Bethlehem Ephrata, are a little one among the thousands of Judah. From you will go forth he who shall be the ruler in Israel, and his landing place has been set from the beginning, from the days of eternity.

verses.context: Through Micah, God tells the small town of Bethlehem that a ruler over Israel, whose origins are from ancient times, will come from it.

KJV.text: For now will I break his yoke from off thee, and will burst thy bonds in sunder.
KJV.displayText: For now will I break his yoke from off thee, and will burst thy bonds in sunder.

BSB.text: For I will now break their yoke from your neck and tear away your shackles.”
BSB.displayText: For I will now break their yoke from your neck and tear away your shackles.”

CPDV.text: And now I will shatter his rod from your back, and I will break open your bonds.
CPDV.displayText: And now I will shatter his rod from your back, and I will break open your bonds.

verses.context: Announcing Nineveh's coming fall, Nahum passes on God's promise to Judah that he will break Assyria's yoke from their neck.

KJV.text: Why dost thou shew me iniquity, and cause me to behold grievance? for spoiling and violence are before me: and there are that raise up strife and contention.
KJV.displayText: Why dost thou shew me iniquity, and cause me to behold grievance? for spoiling and violence are before me: and there are that raise up strife and contention.

BSB.text: Why do You make me see iniquity? Why do You tolerate wrongdoing? Destruction and violence are before me. Strife is ongoing, and conflict abounds.
BSB.displayText: Why do You make me see iniquity? Why do You tolerate wrongdoing? Destruction and violence are before me. Strife is ongoing, and conflict abounds.

CPDV.text: Why have you revealed to me iniquity and hardship, to see plunder and injustice opposite me? And there has been judgment, but the opposition is more powerful.
CPDV.displayText: Why have you revealed to me iniquity and hardship, to see plunder and injustice opposite me? And there has been judgment, but the opposition is more powerful.

verses.context: Watching violence and injustice spread in Judah, the prophet Habakkuk asks God why he makes him see wrongdoing and seems to allow it.

KJV.text: Thou art of purer eyes than to behold evil, and canst not look on iniquity: wherefore lookest thou upon them that deal treacherously, and holdest thy tongue when the wicked devoureth the man that is more righteous than he?
KJV.displayText: Thou art of purer eyes than to behold evil, and canst not look on iniquity: wherefore lookest thou upon them that deal treacherously, and holdest thy tongue when the wicked devoureth the man that is more righteous than he?

BSB.text: Your eyes are too pure to look upon evil, and You cannot tolerate wrongdoing. So why do You tolerate the faithless? Why are You silent while the wicked swallow up those more righteous than themselves?
BSB.displayText: Your eyes are too pure to look upon evil, and You cannot tolerate wrongdoing. So why do You tolerate the faithless? Why are You silent while the wicked swallow up those more righteous than themselves?

CPDV.text: Your eyes are pure, you do not behold evil, and you cannot look towards iniquity. Why do you look upon the agents of iniquity, and remain silent, while the impious is devouring one who is more just than himself?
CPDV.displayText: Your eyes are pure, you do not behold evil, and you cannot look towards iniquity. Why do you look upon the agents of iniquity, and remain silent, while the impious is devouring one who is more just than himself?

verses.context: After God says he will use the ruthless Babylonians to punish Judah, Habakkuk asks how a holy God can stay silent while they devour others.

KJV.text: I will stand upon my watch, and set me upon the tower, and will watch to see what he will say unto me, and what I shall answer when I am reproved.
KJV.displayText: I will stand upon my watch, and set me upon the tower, and will watch to see what he will say unto me, and what I shall answer when I am reproved.

BSB.text: I will stand at my guard post and station myself on the ramparts. I will watch to see what He will say to me, and how I should answer when corrected.
BSB.displayText: I will stand at my guard post and station myself on the ramparts. I will watch to see what He will say to me, and how I should answer when corrected.

CPDV.text: I will stand firm during my watch, and fix my position over the fortification. And I will observe carefully, to see what might be said to me and what I might respond to my opponent.
CPDV.displayText: I will stand firm during my watch, and fix my position over the fortification. And I will observe carefully, to see what might be said to me and what I might respond to my opponent.

verses.context: Having raised his hard questions, Habakkuk says he will take his post on the watchtower and wait to hear how God will answer him.
